memory_update.text: MIDD is the cleanest US-listed reference asset for commercial restaurant equipment and aftermarket/service exposure, but not an underfollowed small-cap.
FARM is a high-relevance but high-risk micro-cap exception: direct coffee/beverage equipment installation, repair, refurbishment, and DSD service network.
WEST belongs in the beverage-complexity second-order lane, but equipment-maintenance exposure is unverified and should not be upgraded without customer/service evidence.

Many pure-play restaurant equipment service networks, parts distributors, Taylor/Henny Penny/Franke service territories, and CFESA repair platforms appear private or non-US-listed; this limits clean public-market mapping.
The service bottleneck may be more about installed-base uptime, factory-certified technicians, parts availability, warranties, and preventative maintenance than new equipment sales alone.

node: Restaurant equipment, beverage-machine service, maintenance, and field support
summary: Expanded the node into a compact two-lane universe. The clearest public-market exposure is Middleby as a commercial foodservice equipment manufacturer with major restaurant-chain relevance and after-sales support. The underfollowed lane is more interesting but lower-evidence: Farmer Brothers has unusually direct beverage-equipment installation/repair exposure but is a micro-cap exception; Westrock Coffee is a small-cap beverage-solutions supplier to foodservice/restaurant customers but equipment-service exposure is not yet proven; Standex has possible residual food-service equipment/specialty-solutions exposure but requires verification because its public narrative is dominated by electronics, engineering, scientific, and engraving segments.
